name.en.note: IUPAC spelling: Aluminium and Caesium replace the American forms of the package

name.zh.note: names fixed by the China National Committee for Terminology in Sciences and Technologies; 113, 115, 117, 118 as announced in 2017

name.de.note: German names in the spelling recommended by the GDCh

mass.citation: J. Meija et al., Atomic weights of the elements 2013 (IUPAC Technical Report), Pure Appl. Chem. 88, 265 (2016); CIAAW tables of standard atomic weights and of radioactive elements (ciaaw.org)
mass.note: standard atomic weight (conventional value where IUPAC gives an interval); cross-checked against periodictable (CIAAW 2021) to 1e-4 relative. Where massIsMassNumber is true the element has no standard atomic weight and the value is the mass number of its most stable isotope as listed by CIAAW

group.note: null for the fifteen lanthanides (57-71) and fifteen actinides (89-103)

block.note: La-Yb and Ac-No are written as f, Lu and Lr as d (IUPAC 2021 provisional recommendation on group 3); the package has La/Ac as d and Lu/Lr as f

category.note: series of the package mapped to keys; lanthanide = 57-71 and actinide = 89-103 (the package counts Lu and Lr as transition metals); polonium is listed as a post-transition metal, not a metalloid

configuration.citation: A. Kramida, Yu. Ralchenko, J. Reader and NIST ASD Team, NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ground states and ionization energies)
configuration.note: ground-state configuration; equal to the NIST ground configuration (ionizationenergies.ground_shells) for every element that table covers, asserted at build time; configurationPredicted marks the elements beyond that table

subshells.note: [n, l, electrons] expanded from the configuration; the electrons sum to z

oxidationStates.citation: Wikipedia, "Oxidation state" (list of oxidation states of the elements), revision 1102394064
oxidationStates.note: common = category "main" of the package, other = category "extended"

electronegativity.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th ed., CRC Press, 2014

radius.atomic.citation: J. C. Slater, Atomic radii in crystals, J. Chem. Phys. 41, 3199 (1964)

radius.covalent.citation: B. Cordero et al., Covalent radii revisited, Dalton Trans. 2008, 2832
radius.covalent.note: single-bond covalent radius, pm; the package averages the three carbon values and the low- and high-spin values of Mn, Fe, Co

radius.covalentDouble.citation: P. Pyykkö, M. Atsumi, Molecular double-bond covalent radii for elements Li–E112, Chem. Eur. J. 15, 12770 (2009)

radius.covalentTriple.citation: P. Pyykkö, S. Riedel, M. Patzschke, Triple-bond covalent radii, Chem. Eur. J. 11, 3511 (2005)

radius.vdw.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th ed., CRC Press, 2014

ionisation.citation: A. Kramida, Yu. Ralchenko, J. Reader and NIST ASD Team, NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ground states and ionization energies)
ionisation.note: first ionisation energy in eV; kJ/mol = eV x 96.4853 (e x N_A, exact SI constants)

electronAffinity.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th ed., CRC Press, 2014; T. Andersen, Atomic negative ions: structure, dynamics and collisions, Phys. Rep. 394, 157 (2004)
electronAffinity.note: eV; negative entries of the package (no stable anion: He, Be, N, Ar, Xe, Yb) and the calculated value for Og are written as null

melt.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 97th ed., CRC Press, 2016
melt.note: K at 101.325 kPa; phase-transition rows are skipped; where several allotropes are listed the one named in "allotrope" is used; null when the substance sublimes

boil.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 97th ed., CRC Press, 2016
boil.note: K at 101.325 kPa; a sublimation point when sublimes is true

density.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th ed., CRC Press, 2014
density.note: g/cm3 near room temperature; gases as ideal-gas density at 25 C and 101.325 kPa (densityPhase says which); the theoretical estimates the package takes from Wikipedia (At, Fr, Es and every element from Fm on) are written as null

state.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 97th ed., CRC Press, 2016
state.note: derived: state at 298.15 K and 101.325 kPa from the melting and boiling (or sublimation) point; null when those are unknown

crystal.citation: N. W. Ashcroft, N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1976 (tables of element crystal structures)
crystal.note: structure type mapped to keys; a as given, b and c computed from the b/a and c/a ratios of the table, angstrom; the table lists diamond for carbon and the hexagonal cell of La, Pr, Nd; selenium and tellurium (c/a far from 1.63) are keyed "hexagonal", not hcp

discovery.note: the package gives no citation for these columns; name spellings and the entries of Be, Nd, Pt, Rn, Bh, Nh, Lv were corrected by hand (DISCOVERY_FIX in build_elements.py); ancient = known since antiquity

abundanceCrust.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th ed., CRC Press, 2014

isotopes.citation: F. G. Kondev et al., The NUBASE2020 evaluation of nuclear physics properties, Chinese Phys. C 45, 030001 (2021); J. Meija et al., Atomic weights of the elements 2013 (IUPAC Technical Report), Pure Appl. Chem. 88, 265 (2016); CIAAW tables of standard atomic weights and of radioactive elements (ciaaw.org)
isotopes.note: isotopes with a natural abundance (percent, representative isotopic composition); cross-checked against periodictable (CIAAW 2021) to 0.2 percentage points; for elements without one, the isotope whose mass number is given as mass, with abundance null

emissionLines.note: textbook value: the flame-test and discharge-tube lines listed in school and first-year texts, nm in air; no installed package provides visible lines, so only these are given and without relative intensities
